reasoning: Torah #116 contains no bechina language in its source text (torah_116.txt). Every conceptual relationship in this Torah is a causal/consequential eitza link. There are no shared-nature identifications that would constitute bechina edges, and therefore no bechina-connected components from which to form packages. The Torah is a 3-line syllogism structured entirely as a causal chain: giving charity → heavenly compassion → receipt of daat → immunity from the spirit of foolishness → immunity from sin. Packages, by definition (see framework.md §3), are formed from bechina-connected nodes only. With zero bechina edges — existing or proposed — no packages can be formed.

structural_note.description: Torah #116 is one of the shortest Torahs in Likutay Moharan Vol. 1 — only 3 lines — and it is structurally a pure eitza chain: a tightly reasoned syllogism connecting four Talmudic principles (Shabbat 151b, Berakhot 33, Sotah 3a) into a single logical argument. This type of Torah has no conceptual 'clusters' of parallel-nature concepts; it has only a linear flow. The teaching is complete as a directed graph of eitza edges. No enrichment of the bechina layer is warranted or possible for this Torah.
structural_note.comparable_structure: Compare to a mathematical proof where each step follows from the previous by logical necessity — there are no synonymous concepts or parallel metaphors, only a chain of 'because... therefore...' statements.
structural_note.good_evil_mirror: No good/evil mirror structure is present. The Torah mentions evil concepts (עֲבֵרָה = sin, רוּחַ שְׁטוּת = spirit of foolishness) but only as terminal conditions being avoided, not as conceptual clusters to be analyzed. They appear as destinations-to-be-avoided in the eitza chain, not as nodes in a bechina network.
structural_note.eitza_chain_completeness: The single existing eitza edge (id: 2176: הנותן צדקה → נצול מעברות) is a valid summary-level eitza that captures the Torah's conclusion. The two intermediate causal steps could optionally be added as additional eitza edges (הנותן צדקה → מרחמין עליו מן השמים, and מרחמין עליו → נותנין לו דעת) but this is an eitza enrichment question, not a bechina/package question.
